shared_elements: low-relief carving cut into a natural stone block
possible animal head rendered in profile
justification: Both are stone surfaces bearing low-relief motifs that include rounded ring or disc forms and curving hook-like lines, and in each a shape can be read as an animal head in profile. But A is a tall, dressed pillar with a disciplined vertical sequence of registers (arched forms, a zigzag band, discrete birds and quadrupeds) carved crisply in pale stone, whereas B is a single rough dark boulder with a small cluster of eroded, ambiguous curvilinear marks and no register system at all.
